metadata.title: Implementing the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Security Rule: A Cybersecurity Resource Guide

prop.name: generated-by

address.addr-line: National Institute of Standards and Technology

part.name: overview
part.p: Defined in the Security Rule as the “administrative actions and policies, and procedures to manage the selection, development, implementation, and maintenance of security measures to protect electronic protected health information and to manage the conduct of the covered entity's workforce in relation to the protection of that information.”

part.name: instruction
part.p: HIPAA Standard: Implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.

control.title: Identify all ePHI and Relevant Information Systems

part.name: description
part.p: Identify where ePHI is generated within the organization, where it enters the organization, where it moves within the organization, where it is stored, and where it leaves the organization.

part.name: description
part.p: Identify all systems that house ePHI. Be sure to identify mobile devices, medical equipment, and medical IoT devices that store, process, or transmit ePHI.

part.name: footnote
part.p: Regulated entities may obtain this information from an organizational business impact assessment (BIA) that has been previously completed. Alternatively, regulated entities can use the information gathered in this activity to create a BIA. See the NISTIR 8286 series of documents for more information

part.name: description
part.p: Include all hardware and software that are used to collect, store, process, or transmit ePHI.

part.name: description
part.p: Analyze business functions and verify the ownership and control of information system elements as necessary.

part.name: description
part.p: Consider the impact of a merger or acquisition on risks to ePHI. During a merger or acquisition, new data pathways may be introduced that lead to ePHI being stored, processed, or transmitted in previously unanticipated places.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has all ePHI generated, stored, processed, and transmitted within the organization been identified?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are all hardware and software for which the organization is responsible periodically inventoried?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is the hardware and software inventory updated on a regular basis?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have hardware and software that maintains or transmits ePHI been identified? Does this inventory include removable media and remote access devices?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is the current configuration of organizational systems documented, including connections to other systems?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has a BIA been performed?

control.title: Conduct Risk Assessment

part.name: description
part.p: Conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of ePHI held by the covered entity or business associate.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are there any prior risk assessments, audit comments, security requirements, and/or security test results?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is there intelligence available from agencies, the Office of the Inspector General (OIG), the US-CERT, virus alerts, and/or vendors?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: What are the human, natural, and environmental threats to systems that contain, store, process, or transmit ePHI?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: What are the current and planned controls?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have likelihood and impact been determined for relevant threats and vulnerabilities?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have risk ratings been determined for relevant threats and vulnerabilities?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is the facility located in a region prone to any natural disasters, such as earthquakes, floods, or fires?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has responsibility been assigned to check all hardware and software – including hardware and software used for remote access – to determine whether selected security settings are enabled?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is there an analysis of current safeguards and their effectiveness relative to the identified risks?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have all processes involving ePHI been considered, including creating, receiving, maintaining, and transmitting it?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 3, Risk Assessment Guidance and Appendix F.

part.name: footnote
part.p: The risks that must be assessed are the risks of noncompliance with the requirements of Section 164.306(a) (General Rules) of the HIPAA Security Rule.

control.title: Implement a Risk Management Program

part.name: description
part.p: Implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level to comply with §164.306(a).

part.name: description
part.p: Risk management should be performed with regular frequency to examine past decisions, reevaluate risk likelihood and impact levels, and assess the effectiveness of past remediation efforts

part.name: description
part.p: Create a Risk Management policy and program that outlines organizational risk appetite and risk tolerance, personnel duties, responsible parties, the frequency of risk management, and required documentation.

part.name: footnote
part.p: See NISTIR 8286, which describes a cybersecurity risk management program in the context of enterprise risk management.

part.name: description
part.p: A risk management methodology is included in Section 4.

part.name: description
part.p: Risk management resources are also included in Appendix F.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is executive leadership and/or management involved in risk management decisions?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has a risk management program been created with related policies?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Does the regulated entity need to engage other resources (e.g., external expertise) to assist in risk management?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Do current safeguards ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of all ePHI?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Do current safeguards protect against reasonably anticipated uses or disclosures of ePHI that are not permitted by the Privacy Rule?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has the regulated entity used the results of risk assessment and risk management processes to guide the selection and implementation of appropriate controls to protect ePHI?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has the regulated entity protected against all reasonably anticipated threats or hazards to the security and integrity of ePHI?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has the regulated entity assured compliance with all policies and procedures by its workforce?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 164.306 of the HIPAA Security Rule and Section 4, Risk Management Guidance.

control.title: Acquire IT Systems and Services

part.name: description
part.p: Regulated entities should consider how cloud services and other third-party IT system and service offerings can both assist regulated entities in protecting ePHI while also potentially introducing new risks to ePHI.

part.name: description
part.p: Although the HIPAA Security Rule does not require purchasing any particular technology, adequately protecting information may require additional hardware, software, or services. Considerations for their selection should include the following:

part.name: description
part.p: Applicability of the IT solution to the intended environment;

part.name: description
part.p: The sensitivity of the data;

part.name: description
part.p: The organization’s security policies, procedures, and standards; and

part.name: description
part.p: Other requirements, such as resources available for operation, maintenance, and training.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Will new security controls work with the existing IT architecture?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have the security requirements of the organization been compared to the security features of existing or proposed hardware and software?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has a cost-benefit analysis been conducted to determine the reasonableness of the investment given the security risks identified?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has a training strategy been developed?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.1.5, HIPAA Standard: Security Awareness and Training.

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 164.306(b) of the HIPAA Security Rule.

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Key Activity 5.1.1.3, Implement a Risk Management Program. This activity and all associated bullets in the Description and Sample Questions are part of the process of addressing the risk management implementation specification.

control.title: Create and Deploy Policies and Procedures

part.name: description
part.p: Implement the decisions concerning the management, operational, and technical controls selected to mitigate identified risks.

part.name: description
part.p: Create policies that clearly establish roles and responsibilities, and assign ultimate responsibility for the implementation of each control to particular individuals or offices.

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.5.1, HIPAA Standard: Policies and Procedures and Section 5.5.2, HIPAA Standard: Documentation.

part.name: description
part.p: Create procedures to be followed to accomplish particular security-related tasks.

part.name: description
part.p: Establish a frequency for reviewing policy and procedures

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has the regulated entity documented an organizational risk assessment/management policy that outlines the duties, responsible parties, frequency, and required documentation of the risk management program?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are policies and procedures in place for security?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is there a formal (documented) system security plan?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is there a formal contingency plan?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.1.7, HIPAA Standard: Contingency Plan.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is there a process for communicating policies and procedures to the affected workforce members?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are policies and procedures reviewed and updated as needed?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Key Activity 5.1.1.3, Implement a Risk Management Program. This activity and all associated bullets in the Description and Sample Questions are part of the process of addressing the risk management implementation specification.

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.5.1, HIPAA Standard: Policies and Procedures.

control.title: Develop and Implement a Sanction Policy

part.name: description
part.p: Apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with the security policies and procedures of the covered entity or business associate

part.name: description
part.p: Develop policies and procedures for imposing appropriate sanctions (e.g., reprimand, termination) for noncompliance with the organization’s security policies.

part.name: description
part.p: Implement sanction policy as cases arise.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Does the regulated entity have existing sanction policies and procedures to meet the requirements of this implementation specification? If not, can existing sanction policies be modified to include language related to violations of these policies and procedures?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is there a formal process in place to address system misuse, abuse, and fraudulent activity?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have workforce members been made aware of policies concerning sanctions for inappropriate access, use, and disclosure of ePHI?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has the need and appropriateness of a tiered structure of sanctions that accounts for the magnitude of harm and possible types of inappropriate disclosures been considered?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: How will managers and workforce members be notified regarding suspect activity?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 164.306 of the HIPAA Security Rule.

control.title: Develop and Deploy the Information System Activity Review Process

part.name: description
part.p: Implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports.

part.name: description
part.p: Implement regular reviews of information system activity, and consider ways to automate the review for the protection of ePHI.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is there a policy that establishes what reviews will be conducted?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are there corresponding procedures that describe the specifics of the reviews?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Who is responsible for the overall process and results?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.1.2, HIPAA Standard: Assigned Security Responsibility.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: How often will reviews take place?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: How often will review results be analyzed?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has the regulated entity considered all available capabilities to automate the reviews?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Where will audit information reside (e.g., separate server)? Will it be stored external to the organization (e.g., cloud service provider)?

control.title: Develop Appropriate Standard Operating Procedures

part.name: description
part.p: Determine the types of audit trail data and monitoring procedures that will be needed to derive exception reports.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: How will exception reports or logs be reviewed?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Where will monitoring reports and their reviews be documented and maintained?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Key Activity 5.1.1.7, Develop and Deploy the Information System Activity Review Process. This activity and all associated bullets in the Description and Sample Questions are part of the process of addressing the information system activity review implementation specification.

control.title: Implement the Information System Activity Review and Audit Process

part.name: description
part.p: Activate the necessary review process.

part.name: description
part.p: Begin auditing and logging activity.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: What mechanisms will be implemented to assess the effectiveness of the review process (measures)?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: What is the plan to revise the review process when needed?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Key Activity 5.1.1.7, Develop and Deploy the Information System Activity Review Process. This activity and all associated bullets in the Description and Sample Questions are part of the process of addressing the information system activity review implementation specification.

part.name: instruction
part.p: HIPAA Standard: Identify the security official who is responsible for the development and implementation of the policies and procedures required by this subpart for the covered entity or business associate.

control.title: Select a Security Official to be Assigned Responsibility for HIPAA Security

part.name: description
part.p: Identify the individual who has final responsibility for security.

part.name: footnote
part.p: While the security officer may enlist help from data governance or security management teams, the Security Rule states that final responsibility must be assigned to one individual.

part.name: description
part.p: Select an individual who is able to assess effective security to serve as the point of contact for security policy, implementation, and monitoring.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Who in the organization:

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Oversees the development and communication of security policies and procedures?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is responsible for conducting the risk assessment?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is responsible for conducting risk management?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Handles the results of periodic security evaluations and continuous monitoring?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Directs IT security purchasing and investment?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Ensures that security concerns have been addressed in system implementation?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Does the security official have adequate access and communications with senior officials in the organization, such as executives, chief information officers, chief compliance officers, and in-house counsel?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Who in the organization is authorized to accept risks from systems on behalf of the organization?

control.title: Assign and Document the Individual’s Responsibility

part.name: description
part.p: Document the assignment to one individual’s responsibilities in a job description.

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.5.2, Standard: Documentation.

part.name: description
part.p: Communicate this assigned role to the entire organization.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is there a complete job description that accurately reflects assigned security duties and responsibilities?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have the staff members in the organization been notified as to whom to call in the event of a security problem?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.1.5, Security Awareness and Training, and Section 5.1.6, Security Incident Procedures.

part.name: instruction
part.p: HIPAA Standard: Implement policies and procedures to ensure that all members of its workforce have appropriate access to electronic protected health information, as provided under paragraph (a)(4) of this section, and to prevent those workforce members who do not have access under paragraph (a)(4) of this section from obtaining access to electronic protected health information.

control.title: Implement Policies and Procedures for Authorization and/or Supervision

part.name: description
part.p: Implement procedures for the authorization and/or supervision of workforce members who work with ePHI or in locations where it might be accessed.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have chains of command and lines of authority been established?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have staff members been made aware of the identity and roles of their supervisors?

control.title: Establish Clear Job Descriptions and Responsibilities

part.name: description
part.p: Define roles and responsibilities for all job functions.

part.name: description
part.p: Assign appropriate levels of security oversight, training, and access.

part.name: description
part.p: Identify in writing who has the business need and who has been granted permission to view, alter, retrieve, and store ePHI and at what times, under what circumstances, and for what purposes.

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.5.2, HIPAA Standard: Documentation.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are there written job descriptions that are correlated with appropriate levels of access to ePHI?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are these job descriptions reviewed and updated on a regular basis?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have staff members been provided copies of their job descriptions and informed of the access granted to them, as well as the conditions by which this access can be used

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Key Activity 5.1.3.1, Implement Policies and Procedures for Authorization and/or Supervision. This activity and all associated bullets in the Description and Sample Questions are part of the procedures for authorization and/or supervision.

control.title: Establish Criteria and Procedures for Hiring and Assigning Tasks

part.name: description
part.p: Ensure that staff members have the necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities to fulfill particular roles (e.g., positions involving access to and use of sensitive information).

part.name: description
part.p: Ensure that these requirements are included as part of the personnel hiring process.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have the qualifications of candidates for specific positions been checked against the job description?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have determinations been made that candidates for specific positions are able to perform the tasks of those positions?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Key Activity 5.1.3.1, Implement Policies and Procedures for Authorization and/or Supervision. This activity and all associated bullets in the Description and Sample Questions are part of the procedures for authorization and/or supervision.

control.title: Establish a Workforce Clearance Procedure

part.name: description
part.p: Implement procedures to determine that the access of a workforce member to ePHI is appropriate.

part.name: description
part.p: Implement appropriate screening of persons who will have access to ePHI.

part.name: description
part.p: Implement a procedure for obtaining clearance from appropriate offices or individuals where access is provided or terminated.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is there an implementation strategy that supports the designated access authorities?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are applicants’ employment and educational references checked, if reasonable and appropriate?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have background checks been completed, if reasonable and appropriate?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are there procedures for determining that the appropriate workforce members have access to the necessary information?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Do procedures exist for obtaining appropriate sign-offs to grant or terminate access to ePHI?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have clearance and supervision procedures been developed for non-US based workforce members that are applicable to their location?

control.title: Establish Termination Procedures

part.name: description
part.p: Implement procedures for terminating access to ePHI when the employment of or other arrangement with a workforce member ends or as required by determinations made as specified in §164.308(a)(3)(ii)(B).

part.name: description
part.p: Develop a standard set of procedures that should be followed to recover access control devices (e.g., identification badges, keys, access cards) when employment ends.

part.name: description
part.p: Deactivate computer access accounts (e.g., disable user IDs and passwords) and facility access (e.g., change facility security codes/PINs).

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.3.1, HIPAA Standard: Access Control.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are there separate procedures for voluntary termination (e.g., retirement, promotion, transfer, change of employment) versus involuntary termination (e.g., termination for cause, reduction in force, involuntary transfer, criminal or disciplinary actions), if reasonable and appropriate?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is there a standard checklist for all action items that should be completed when a workforce member leaves (e.g., return of all access devices, deactivation of logon accounts .including remote access, and delivery of any needed data solely under the employee’s control)?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Do other organizations need to be notified to deactivate accounts that the workforce member had access to in the performance of their employment duties?

part.name: instruction
part.p: HIPAA Standard: Implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to electronic protected health information that are consistent with the applicable requirements of subpart E of this part.

part.name: footnote
part.p: See also Section 5.2.1, HIPAA Standard: Facility Access Controls and Section 5.3.1, HIPAA Standard: Access Control.

control.title: Isolate Healthcare Clearinghouse Functions

part.name: description
part.p: If a healthcare clearinghouse is part of a larger organization, the clearinghouse must implement policies and procedures that protect the ePHI of the clearinghouse from unauthorized access by the larger organization.

part.name: description
part.p: Determine whether a component of the regulated entity constitutes a healthcare clearinghouse under the HIPAA Security Rule.

part.name: description
part.p: If no clearinghouse functions exist, document this finding. If a clearinghouse exists within the organization, implement procedures for access that are consistent with the HIPAA Privacy Rule.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: If healthcare clearinghouse functions are performed, are policies and procedures implemented to protect ePHI from the other functions of the larger organization?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Does the healthcare clearinghouse share hardware or software with a larger organization of which it is a part?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Does the healthcare clearinghouse share staff or physical space with staff from a larger organization?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has a separate network or subsystem been established for the healthcare clearinghouse, if reasonable and appropriate?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has staff of the healthcare clearinghouse been trained to safeguard ePHI from disclosure to the larger organization, if required for compliance with the HIPAA Privacy Rule?

part.name: footnote
part.p: Where the healthcare clearinghouse is a separate legal entity, it is subject to the Security Rule whether or not the larger organization is a covered entity.

control.title: Implement Policies and Procedures for Authorizing Access

part.name: description
part.p: Implement policies and procedures for granting access to ePHI, such as through access to a workstation, transaction, program, process, or other mechanism.

part.name: description
part.p: Decide and document procedures for how access to ePHI will be granted to workforce members within the organization.

part.name: description
part.p: Select the basis for restricting access to ePHI.

part.name: description
part.p: Select an access control method (e.g., identity-based, role-based, or other reasonable and appropriate means of access.)

part.name: description
part.p: Decide and document how access to ePHI will be granted for privileged functions.

part.name: description
part.p: Ensure that there is a list of personnel with authority to approve user requests to access ePHI and systems with ePHI.

part.name: description
part.p: Identify authorized users with access to ePHI, including data owners and data custodians.

part.name: description
part.p: Consider whether multiple access control methods are needed to protect ePHI according to the results of the risk assessment.

part.name: description
part.p: Determine whether direct access to ePHI will ever be appropriate for individuals external to the organization (e.g., business partners or patients seeking access to their own ePHI).

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have appropriate authorization and clearance procedures, as specified in Workforce Security (§ 164.308(a)(3)), been performed prior to granting access?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Do the organization’s systems have the capacity to set access controls?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.3.1, HIPAA Standard: Access Control.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are there documented job descriptions that accurately reflect assigned duties and responsibilities and enforce segregation of duties?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.1.3, HIPAA Standard: Workforce Security.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Has the organization documented procedures that specify how authorized personnel will be granted access to ePHI?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Does the organization grant remote access to ePHI?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: What methods of access control are used (e.g., identity-based, role-based, location-based, or a combination) to protect ePHI?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are there additional access control requirements for users who will be accessing privileged functions?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Have organizational personnel been explicitly authorized to approve user requests to access ePHI and/or systems with ePHI?

control.title: Implement Policies and Procedures for Access Establishment and Modification

part.name: description
part.p: Implement policies and procedures that – based on the covered entity or business associate’s access authorization policies – establish, document, review, and modify a user's right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process.

part.name: description
part.p: Establish standards for granting access to ePHI.

part.name: description
part.p: Provide formal authorization from the appropriate authority before granting access to ePHI.

part.name: description
part.p: Regularly review personnel access to ePHI to ensure that access is still authorized and needed.

part.name: description
part.p: Modify personnel access to ePHI, as needed, based on review activities.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are duties separated such that only the minimum necessary ePHI is made available to each workforce member based on their job requirements?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are access decisions justified, approved, logged, and retained?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is personnel access to ePHI regularly reviewed to ensure that access is still authorized and needed?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are activities that review access to ePHI logged and retained, including decisions that arise from review activities?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are decisions related to the establishment and modification of workforce member authorization to access ePHI documented?

control.title: Evaluate Existing Security Measures Related to Access Controls

part.name: description
part.p: Evaluate the security features of access controls that are already in place or those of any planned for implementation, as appropriate.

part.name: description
part.p: Determine whether these security features involve alignment with other existing management, operational, and technical controls, such as policy standards, personnel procedures, the maintenance and review of audit trails, the identification and authentication of users, and physical access controls.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are there policies and procedures related to the security of access controls? If so, are they updated regularly?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.5.2, HIPAA Section: Documentation.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are authentication mechanisms used to verify the identity of those accessing systems protected from inappropriate manipulation?

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.3.4, HIPAA Standard: Person or Entity Authentication.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Does management regularly review the list of access authorizations, including remote access authorizations, to verify that the list is accurate and has not been inappropriately altered?.1

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.1.3, HIPAA Standard: Workforce Security.

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Key Activity 5.1.4.3, Implement Policies and Procedures for Access Establishment and Modification. This activity and all associated bullets in the Description and Sample Questions are part of the access establishment and modification implementation specification.

part.name: instruction
part.p: HIPAA Standard: Implement a security awareness and training program for all members of its workforce (including management).

part.name: footnote
part.p: See also Section 5.2.1, HIPAA Standard: Facility Access Controls; Section 5.3.1, HIPAA Standard: Access Control; and Appendix F.

control.title: Conduct a Training Needs Assessment

part.name: description
part.p: Determine the training needs of the organization.

part.name: description
part.p: Interview and involve key personnel in assessing security training needs.

part.name: description
part.p: Use feedback and analysis of past events to help determine training needs

part.name: description
part.p: Review organizational behavior issues, past incidents, and/or breaches to determine what training is missing or needs reinforcement, improvement, or periodic reminders.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: What awareness, training, and education programs are needed? Which are required?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is the organization monitoring current threats to determine possible areas of training needs?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Are there current, relevant threats (e.g., phishing, ransomware) about which personnel need training?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Do workforce members need training on any particular organization devices (e.g., medical IoT) or technology that pose a risk to ePHI?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: What is the current status regarding how these needs are being addressed (e.g., how well are current efforts working)?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Where are the gaps between the needs and what is being done (e.g., what more needs to be done)?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: What are the training priorities in terms of content and audience?

control.title: Develop and Approve a Training Strategy and a Plan

part.name: description
part.p: Address the specific HIPAA policies that require security awareness and training in the security awareness and training program.

part.name: description
part.p: Set organizational expectations for protecting ePHI.

part.name: description
part.p: In the security awareness and training program, outline the program’s scope, goals, target audiences, learning objectives, deployment methods, and evaluation and measurement techniques, as well as the frequency of training

part.name: sample_question
part.p: Is there a procedure in place to ensure that everyone in the organization receives security awareness training, including teleworkers and remote personnel?

part.name: sample_question

group.title: Business Associate Contracts or Other Arrangements

prop.name: label
prop.value: Business Associate Contracts or Other Arrangements (164.314(a))

part.name: instruction
part.p: HIPAA Standard: (i) The contract or other arrangement between the covered entity and its business associate required by § 164.308(b)(3) must meet the requirements of paragraph (a)(2)(i), (a)(2)(ii), or (a)(2)(iii) of this section, as applicable. (ii) A covered entity is in compliance with paragraph (a)(1) of this section if it has another arrangement in place that meets the requirements of § 164.504(e)(3). (iii) The requirements of paragraphs (a)(2)(i) and (a)(2)(ii) of this section apply to the contract or other arrangement between a business associate and a subcontractor required by § 164.308(b)(4) in the same manner as such requirements apply to contracts or other arrangements between a covered entity and business associate.

control.title: Contract Must Provide that Business Associates Will Comply with the Applicable Requirements of the Security Rule

part.name: description
part.p: Contracts between covered entities and business associates must provide that business associates will implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the ePHI that the business associate creates, receives, maintains, or transmits on behalf of the covered entity.

group.title: Policies and Procedures and Documentation Requirements

prop.name: label
prop.value: Policies and Procedures and Documentation Requirements (164.316)

part.name: overview
part.p: Requires the implementation of reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the standards, implementation specifications, and other requirements of the Security Rule; the maintenance of written (may be electronic) documentation and/or records that include the policies, procedures, actions, activities, or assessments required by the Security Rule; and retention, availability, and update requirements related to the documentation.

part.name: instruction
part.p: HIPAA Standard: Implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the standards, implementation specifications, or other requirements of this subpart, taking into account those factors specified in § 164.306(b)(2)(i), (ii), (iii), and (iv). This standard is not to be construed to permit or excuse an action that violates any other standard, implementation specification, or other requirements of this subpart. A covered entity or business associate may change its policies and procedures at any time, provided that the changes are documented and are implemented in accordance with this subpart.

control.title: Create and Deploy Policies and Procedures

part.name: description
part.p: Implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the standards, implementation specifications, and other requirements of the HIPAA Security Rule.

part.name: description
part.p: Consider the importance of documenting processes and procedures for demonstrating the adequate implementation of recognized security practices.

part.name: description
part.p: Periodically evaluate written policies and procedures to verify that:

part.name: description
part.p: Policies and procedures are sufficient to address the standards, implementation specifications, and other requirements of the HIPAA Security Rule.

part.name: description
part.p: Policies and procedures accurately reflect the actual activities and practices exhibited by the regulated entity, its staff, its systems, and its business associates.

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.1.8, HIPAA Standard: Evaluation.

part.name: sample_question
part.p: The costs for security measures?

part.name: sample_question
part.p: The probability and criticality of potential risks to ePHI?

control.title: Update the Documentation of the Policy and Procedures

part.name: description
part.p: Change policies and procedures as is reasonable and appropriate at any time, provided that the changes are documented and implemented in accordance with the requirements of the HIPAA Security Rule.

part.name: footnote
part.p: See Section 5.5.2, HIPAA Standard: Documentation and Section 5.1.5, HIPAA Standard: Security Awareness and Training.

part.name: instruction
part.p: HIPAA Standard: (i) Maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with this subpart in written (which may be electronic) form; and (ii) if an action, activity or assessment is required by this subpart to be documented, maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of the action, activity, or assessment.

control.title: Draft, Maintain, and Update Required Documentation

part.name: description
part.p: Document decisions concerning the management, operational, and technical controls selected to mitigate identified risks.

part.name: description
part.p: Written documentation may be incorporated into existing manuals, policies, and other documents or be created specifically for the purpose of demonstrating compliance with the HIPAA Security Rule.

part.name: description

part.name: description
part.p: Use feedback from risk assessments and contingency plan tests to help determine when to update documentation.

control.title: Retain Documentation for at Least Six Years

part.name: description
part.p: Retain documentation required by paragraph (b)(1) of this section for six years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.

part.name: description
part.p: Make documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.

part.name: description
part.p: Review documentation periodically and update as needed in response to environmental or operational changes that affect the security of the ePHI.
